goal: Make Kryos functional and adoptable: prove the governed agent is a portable embeddable unit (native + WASM + C-ABI) carrying its @budget/@capabilities/Tracked guarantees, and close real correctness bugs. Build-plane only.
ordering: Work top-to-bottom; the list is ordered easiest-first so each iteration can land a real, committed increment. Bank wins. Never regress the cargo suite. Partial progress is fine: commit whatever compiles+improves each iteration, even if the feature's check.sh does not yet pass.
mock_llm_rule: All demos MUST use a deterministic MOCK LLM (a tiny stub fn that returns a canned answer + a fixed token/cost count). NO live API calls, NO creds, NO spend. The point is to prove governance + portability, not a real model round-trip.

features.title: Governed agent embedded in a native Kryos program
features.contract: START HERE. Build ONE small governed agent in demo/agent/ (reused by all hosts): takes a question, calls a MOCK LLM stub, returns an answer plus its source string. The agent fn is annotated @budget(usd=...) and @capabilities(net:http). First make it run with `kryos run`, then `kryos build --release`. Create demo/native/check.sh that asserts deterministically: (a) a within-budget call returns the answer WITH its source; (b) an over-budget call is refused BEFORE the mock LLM records spend (assert a refusal value / unchanged spend counter); (c) a negative-control .kry where a fn calls the mock LLM WITHOUT declaring net capability FAILS to compile under --strict-capabilities (assert non-zero compile + the E05xx capability error). Commit partial progress each iteration. Read the repo CLAUDE.md for Kryos syntax first.

features.title: Same governed agent compiled to WASM
features.contract: Compile the SAME demo/agent governed agent to wasm32 (kryos build --release --backend wasm) and run it via `node tools/wasm-host/run.mjs`. The mock LLM must be wasm-safe (pure compute or routed through the JS host; the native HTTPS stdlib will NOT link in wasm). demo/wasm/check.sh asserts the within-budget answer+source and the over-budget refusal are observable from the wasm run. If a genuine wasm-backend limitation blocks it, fix the wasm backend OR shrink the agent to the wasm-supported subset and document the exact gap in demo/wasm/NOTES.md; the gate only passes when the demo actually runs in wasm.

features.title: Same governed agent called via the C ABI from a non-Kryos host
features.contract: Expose the demo/agent governed agent through the C ABI (kryos bindgen / an extern entry point), build it as a static lib, and call it from a tiny C harness compiled with clang, linking the kryos runtime libs. demo/cabi/check.sh builds the lib + the C harness, runs it, and asserts the within-budget answer+source and the over-budget refusal hold when driven from C. Document the exact link recipe in demo/cabi/NOTES.md.

features.title: In-place mutation of aggregates inside collections (deep compiler fix)
features.contract: Hard compiler fix; do this only when the embeds are progressing. Fix `arr[i].field = v` and `m[k].field = v` so the mutated element is written back / mutated in place, correct on BOTH backends (kryos run AND kryos build --release), for stack-promoted literal arrays (let mut xs=[..]) AND heap/push-built arrays AND maps. Root cause: lower_nested_field_assign's IndexAccess fallback (compiler/crates/kryos-mir/src/lower.rs) mutates a throwaway copy with no write-back. Correct fix = in-place mutation through the element box pointer (works for stack+heap). A naive kryos_array_set write-back crashes stack arrays - do NOT reintroduce that. demo/mutation/check.sh builds+runs a .kry covering all three cases on both backends and asserts exact values.

features.title: Harden the compiler: adversarial probe corpus, both backends agree
features.contract: The four embed/mutation milestones already PASS. This is now a REAL gate: build an adversarial probe corpus under tests/harden-probes/ that stresses the compiler and proves both backends agree. Each iteration: (1) ADD several NEW small deterministic probes (.kry that prints fixed output) to tests/harden-probes/ targeting UNDER-tested construct COMBINATIONS -- nested generics (Box<Wrap<i64>>), trait objects in arrays/maps, closures stored in maps and returned from match arms, enums whose payload is a struct/tuple/array, map<K, aggregate> mutation + iteration, deep struct nesting (a.b.c.d.field), Option/Result of aggregates through HOFs, channel-send of an aggregate, recursion with aggregate accumulators, string-interp of computed aggregates. (2) Run each on BOTH `kryos run` AND `kryos build --release`. (3) If a probe CRASHES or the two backends DISAGREE, that is a real bug: FIX it in the compiler (compiler/crates/kryos-mir/src/lower.rs, kryos-codegen-llvm/src/codegen.rs, kryos-codegen-cranelift/src/codegen.rs) -- JIT is usually the oracle, AOT usually the offender (allocator/ABI/box-unbox). NEVER delete or weaken a probe to make the gate pass, and NEVER weaken the cargo suite. (4) Commit every iteration. The gate passes at >= 48 probes all agreeing on both backends with the cargo suite green; that is a meaningfully hardened compiler. The first 24 probes (probe_01..probe_24) already pass; ADD 24 MORE that are HARDER (probe_25+): genuinely try to break AOT with combinatorial aggregate cases the first 24 did not cover. Allocator convention reminder: aggregate boxing in collections/enum-payloads/closure-captures uses kryos_calloc (matches kryos_free), NOT kryos_arc_alloc_*; closure aggregate args forward as ptr byval(%Agg).
